summary: Comfort, comfort my people, cry to Jerusalem warfare ended, iniquity pardoned. Voice crying in wilderness prepare way of Yahweh, every valley lifted, mountain made low. All flesh is grass, grass withers flower fades but word of our God stands forever. Behold Lord comes with might, like shepherd tends flock, gathers lambs in arms. Who has measured waters? To whom will you liken God? Idols vs Creator, He gives power to faint.
whyItMatters: Pivot in Isaiah from judgment (1-39) to comfort (40-66). Most quoted hope chapters — Handel's Messiah opens with Comfort, John the Baptist's voice in wilderness, New Testament quotes word stands forever, shepherd and creator vs idols.

context.author: Isaiah or Second Isaiah
context.setting: Exile, needing comfort that warfare ended
context.literaryForm: Proclamation of comfort with two contrasting voices: comforter and wilderness crier

outline.heading: Comfort — warfare ended, iniquity pardoned, double for sins
Voice — prepare way in wilderness, glory revealed, all flesh grass
Behold God — shepherd, Creator who measures waters
He gives power to faint — wait on Yahweh renew strength

keyVerses.text: “Comfort, comfort my people,” says your God.
keyVerses.why: Opening command — comfort, comfort my people — double for emphasis.

keyVerses.text: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.”
keyVerses.why: Contrast perishable humanity vs enduring word.

keyVerses.text: Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard? The everlasting God, Yahweh, the Creator of the ends of the earth, doesn’t faint. He isn’t weary. His understanding is unsearchable.
keyVerses.why: Ending promise — faint to power, waiting not wasting.

questions.question: Why 'Comfort, comfort my people — warfare ended, she has received double for all her sins'?
questions.answer: Israel's 70-year exile felt like double punishment. Prophet says speak tenderly to Jerusalem — warfare (time of hard service) accomplished, iniquity pardoned, she received from Lord double? Some read double punishment already received, now comfort; others double grace. Either way, emphasis is sufficient payment, time to comfort not just judge.

questions.question: What does 'voice crying in wilderness prepare way of Yahweh' mean?
questions.answer: Wilderness is where Israel wandered and where exile road back. Prepare way like ancient practice: before king visits, road builders fill valleys, lower mountains, straighten crooked. John the Baptist applies to himself (John 1:23): preparing way for Lord's arrival. Every valley lifted, mountain low — leveling for King's arrival, moral and literal.

questions.question: Why 'all flesh is grass, grass withers flower fades but word of God stands forever'?
questions.answer: Human glory like grass beauty brief, especially in exile where empire seems permanent. Word stands forever contrasts human frailty with divine promise's durability. New Testament (1 Peter 1:24-25) quotes this to say gospel is that enduring word. Comfort is not in human strength enduring but word enduring.

questions.question: What does 'He will feed his flock like a shepherd, gather lambs in his arms' mean after Creator measuring waters?
questions.answer: Chapter juxtaposes transcendence (who measured waters in hollow of hand, heavens with span, weighed mountains) with intimacy (shepherd gathers lambs, carries close to heart, gently leads nursing ewes). Both true: incomprehensibly big and tenderly near. Anti-idol polemic: idols can't do either, they need to be carried.

questions.question: What does 'wait on Yahweh shall renew strength, mount up with wings like eagles' mean? Is waiting passive?
questions.answer: Hebrew qavah = wait, hope, expect, like farmer waits for rain. Not passive sitting but active expecting, like braiding rope — renew strength, change strength. Youths faint, young men stumble, but those waiting exchange strength — run not weary, walk not faint. Famous for encouragement: waiting is not wasting but exchanging tiredness for God's strength.

glossary.def: Hebrew nacham — comfort, console, with doublet for emphasis.
Royal road-building before king's visit — fill, lower, straighten.
Wait, hope, expect, braid together — active expectancy exchanging strength.
